sectors.trend: Iron ore price collapse pressures BHP and peers; small-cap miners (Kaoko, Vanadium, Piche, Aurum, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals) outperform on speculative flows; Aureka's $8.9M Victorian acquisition signals consolidation at low valuations
sectors.implications: Large-cap miners face margin compression; small-cap gold and critical-mines names attract risk-on capital. BHP strategic review may signal M&A or capital return shifts

sectors.trend: Oil price rise and tanker-war tensions support Woodside, Santos, and oil-services names; Valaris returns to profit on offshore activity
sectors.implications: Energy is today's ASX outperformer; sustained oil strength supports WDS.AX, STO.AX, and upstream E&P valuations

sectors.trend: Accelerating housing price falls and RBA's refusal to cut rates create credit-risk overhang for banks and REITs; property developer workforce suspensions signal construction downturn
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX face rising NPL pressure; REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) under pressure; construction names (WTC.AX, CGW.AX) at risk

sectors.trend: Mortgage costs push households into second jobs; consumer sentiment weakens; BYD's EV dominance disrupts auto retail
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WBC.AX, and retail names face subdued discretionary spending; auto dealers under structural pressure from BYD

sectors.trend: BYD declares Australia EV tipping point passed; AI and tech themes (Snowflake, Anthropic) drive global risk appetite
sectors.implications: ASX-listed EV infrastructure and charging names benefit; global AI momentum supports CSL.AX-adjacent tech and SSG.AX

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely range-bound to slightly lower; energy offsets materials weakness. Housing data and RBA commentary dominate. Small-cap mining volatility elevated. Consumer names under pressure from mortgage stress.
market_outlook.long_term: Structural headwinds from iron ore cycle peak and housing correction weigh on ^AXJO. Energy and gold offer relative strength. EV transition and AI themes provide medium-term growth pockets. RBA unlikely to ease, keeping rate-sensitive sectors suppressed.
